rule: The rows file has exactly the columns Account, Date, Description, Type, Amount, Own transfer and the balances file Account, Month, Printed opening, Printed closing
why it matters: Columns are read by name. A missing one silently drops a whole check.

rule: Dates are YYYY-MM-DD and months YYYY-MM
why it matters: Mixed date formats put rows in the wrong month and break the daily balances.

rule: Type is one of Deposit, Withdrawal, Fee, Check, Interest, Transfer
why it matters: NSF counts come from Fee rows and transfer checks from Transfer rows. An unknown type falls through both.

rule: Amounts are plain signed numbers with two decimals
why it matters: A dollar sign or thousands comma turns a number into text and drops it from every total.

rule: The sign agrees with the type: deposits and interest positive; withdrawals, fees and checks negative
why it matters: A flipped sign moves money from deposits to withdrawals and changes the average a lender reads.

rule: Own transfer is Yes or blank
why it matters: Only Yes takes a row out of business deposits. Anything else is ambiguous.

rule: Each month's printed opening plus its rows equals its printed closing
why it matters: This is the proof that no row or page is missing. No analysis is produced until every month ties.

rule: Each month's printed opening equals the previous month's printed closing
why it matters: A break means a mistyped balance or a statement for the wrong period.

rule: Every account has printed balances for every month from its first to its last, and no rows fall outside them
why it matters: A month with rows but no balances can't be proven. A month with no statement is a hole in the analysis.

rule: Every row tagged as an own transfer has an opposite row in another account of the file within 3 days
why it matters: Tagging an outside deposit as an own transfer hides income. Matching both sides proves the money only moved.

rule: Transfer rows are tagged, or confirmed as outside money
why it matters: An untagged transfer counts as business money. If it came from the owner's personal account, deposits are overstated by that amount.
